provenance.l: Planned RESILIENCE landing sequence (Spaceflight Now, 6 Jun 2025): coast from 100 km to 20 km, main braking from 20 km to 3 km and from about 6,000 to 380 km/h, then pitch-over and a terminal descent to 100 m. The model starts the braking at 20 km and 1,667 m/s and ends it at 3.0 km and 106 m/s

Last telemetry about 192 m (630 ft) above the surface, faster than expected, about 1 min 45 s before the scheduled touchdown (Space.com; SpacePolicyOnline reads 1:40 off a simulation display). The speed is unresolved in the sources (about 42 m/s; a 187 km/h figure also circulates): the model holds 42 m/s from the end of the braking to the ground
ispace technical cause analysis (24 Jun 2025): the laser range finder was slow to give valid altitudes, so the lander could not slow down enough
NASA LRO: the impact site at 60.4445 N, 355.4120 E, a dark smudge with a subtle bright halo (LROC 1456)

estimatedFields: brakingMaxThrustN (fitted so the braking ends near 3 km at 380 km/h, as planned; the engine's thrust is not published)
terminalVelocityMs (the unresolved 42 m/s, held from the end of the braking)
